data.title: Waste Connections & Deep Fission enter Utilities Russell 3000 Index
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of companies set to join or leave the Russell 3000 Index as part of its 2026 annual reconstitution.

The utilities companies set to join the index include: Waste Connections (WCN) and Deep Fission (FISN).

No companies in the utilities sector were removed from the index. 

The final inclusion is expected to take effect after the U.S. market opens on  December 4, 2026, as part of the Russell indexes’ annual reconstitution, effective after market close on December 11, 2026.

data.title: Hedge funds divided on Uber Technologies in Q3
data.description:
Uber Technologies (UBER) had a mixed Q3 with a major fund manager cutting its entire stake in the company even as some investors raised their holding. Some major fund managers also held on to their shares, avoiding any activity in the quarter.

George Soros' Soros Fund exited its 90,000 shares in Uber in Q3.

Tiger Global maintained its 151,000 stake in the ride-hailing app. Pershing Square also held on to its 34.27M shares in the company through the quarter.

Altimeter added more Uber shares to its portfolio, raising its stake to 8.81M shares from 7.37M in Q3. Glenview Capital took its stock holding to 2.09Mfrom 1.79M  shares in the quarter.

Appaloosa cut its exposure in Uber to 7.32M from 7.69M shares. 

Uber's stock price has dropped over 23% in the past year, with Q3 seeing some volatility. Shares jumped to as high as $80 in August but plunged back to nearly $68.5 by September end. Seeking Alpha and Wall Street analysts rated the stock a Buy.

data.title: Utilities firms Net Power & Deep Fission join Russel Microcap; Spruce Power removed
data.description:
FTSE Russell has published preliminary lists of companies to be added to or removed from the Russell Microcap Indexes.

Utilities firms that were added to the index include: Net Power (NPWR) and Deep Fission (FISN).

Only one utility company was deleted from the index, Spruce Power Holding (SPRU).

The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the US market close on December 11.

data.title: Geospace outlines path to profitability in fiscal 2027 with backlog exceeding $100M
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Geospace Technologies (GEOS) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • "For the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, we reported revenue of $19.6 million with a net loss of $13.7 million." (President, CEO & Director Richard Kelley)
  • "The management team took decisive steps to realign our operations, reduce costs and position Geospace for a return to profitability." (President, CEO & Director Kelley) "During this fiscal year, we implemented 2 reductions in force, and early retirement program and cutbacks in operating expenses to better align our cost structure with today's business environment." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "Disappointing revenue declines in our Smart Water segment were driven predominantly by decreases in orders for our Hydroconn line of smart water meter connector cables." (President, CEO & Director Kelley) "At the end of the year, we ended a decade-long relationship with an external manufacturing representative firm who had exclusively marketed the Hydroconn connectors." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "In fiscal year 2027, we will change our market strategy and use internal sales and marketing resources to build demand and secure specifications of our products in utility AMI-related procurements." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "The segment focused resources on execution of sizable contracts, including the Petrobras's Permanent Reservoir Monitoring or PRM program, which is expected to be shipped and product-related revenue recognized by the end of fiscal year 2027." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "After a lengthy effort and as previously announced, our Quantum Technology Sciences subsidiary entered into a $10.8 million contract with the U.S. Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane division for the company's Seismic Acoustic Detection and Ranging Underwater System." (President, CEO & Director Kelley) "We anticipate revenue recognition from the project to span fiscal years 2027 and 2028." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "We entered fiscal year 2027 with a backlog exceeding $100 million from contracts across our 3 segments." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "Before I begin, I'd like to remind everyone that we will not provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance during our call this morning." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Robert Curda)

Outlook

  • "We will not provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance during our call this morning." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • "The Petrobras's Permanent Reservoir Monitoring or PRM program... is expected to be shipped and product-related revenue recognized by the end of fiscal year 2027." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "We anticipate revenue recognition in our fiscal Q1 and Q2 and Q3." (President, CEO & Director Kelley) "We should recognize the majority of the goods revenue associated with that contract in the fiscal year." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • "Our anticipation for Q1 is similar to what we've experienced in prior Q1... we do see a bit of a softening in demand." (President, CEO & Director Kelley) "Our real expectation for returning profitability would be closer to Q2 and Q3." (President, CEO & Director Kelley) "Our intent to return to full profitability by the end of the fiscal year." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)

Financial Results

  • "We reported revenue of $19.6 million compared to last year's revenue of $30.7 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda) "The net loss for the quarter was $13.7 million or $1.06 per diluted share." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • "Our fourth quarter loss include noncash charges of $3.5 million in cumulative translation losses from our Colombian operation and $2.9 million of underutilized assets related to select nodal rental tools and manufacturing equipment." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • "For the 12 months ended September 30, 2026, we reported revenue of $80.7 million." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda) "Our net loss for the 12-month period was $44.3 million or $3.43 per diluted share." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • "Revenue from our Smart Water segment totaled $3.1 million" in Q4 fiscal 2026 and "$17.2 million" for fiscal 2026. (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • "Revenue from our Energy Solutions segment totaled $10.8 million" in Q4 fiscal 2026 and "$40.9 million" for fiscal 2026. (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • "Revenue from our Intelligent Industrial segment totaled $5.6 million" in Q4 fiscal 2026 and "$22.2 million" for fiscal 2026. (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • "At September 30, we had working capital of $43.6 million, which includes $14 million of trade accounts and financing receivables." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda) "On October 29, we entered into a revolving loan and security agreement with Amerisource Funding Inc., restructuring and terminating our Woodforest credit agreement." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda) "At this time, we have approximately $13 million of available borrowings under the Amerisource agreement." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)

Q&A

  • Isaac Pommer, Tieton Capital Management: asked Petrobras PRM revenue in the September quarter and the expected cadence; Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda: "It wasn't that significant. It's about $6.5 million." President, CEO & Director Kelley: "we anticipate revenue recognition in our fiscal Q1 and Q2 and Q3" and Curda added, "It should continue to grow and come to its peak in our Q2 and come to an end in Q3."
  • Isaac Pommer, Tieton Capital Management: asked about PRM tenders and visibility; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "None that we're discussing now" and "everything we discuss with our clients is considered confidential... we're not able to make a comment at this time."
  • Isaac Pommer, Tieton Capital Management: asked about cost-savings and the expense rate; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "we reduced our overhead -- overall headcount by over 10% in fiscal year 2026" and "we're also utilizing a lot of AI productivity tools to try to reduce the amount of manual labor within the organization."
  • Isaac Pommer, Tieton Capital Management: pressed for near-term direction; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "our anticipation for Q1 is similar" and "flattish... More profitability in Q2 and Q3 with our intent to return to full profitability by the end of the fiscal year."
  • Michael Cox: challenged liquidity, leverage, and the ability to reach milestone cash receipts; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "we anticipate a cash infusion in early Q2" and "we do anticipate being able to bridge between where we are today and that next infusion of cash from Petrobras."
  • Michael Cox: questioned Petrobras change orders and payment timing; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "Petrobras had made some changes to the design... That's all behind us" and "until we hit that milestone, we can't expect another infusion of cash."
  • Michael Cox: asked about revolver availability; Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda: "There's limitations on the borrowing base... we may not have the base available to borrow the full amount."
  • Michael Cox: asked for liquidity “plan B”; Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda: "We're continuing to evaluate those options... they're definitely not off the table."
  • Sheldon Grodsky, Grodsky Associates, Inc.: asked about financing receivables; Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda: "The majority of the financing receivables we have a maturity of about 24 months left on them" and "that's actually one of the ones that's on the table also" as a liquidity option.
  • Sheldon Grodsky, Grodsky Associates, Inc.: asked about rental fleet strategy; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "we certainly still plan to be in the rental equipment business for marine nodes" and "the older legacy equipment, the OBX product line, we are phasing that out, and we anticipate standardizing around the Mariner solution."
  • Sheldon Grodsky, Grodsky Associates, Inc.: asked about acquisitions under the new credit agreement; Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda: "Our current credit agreement doesn't prohibit us for making acquisitions" and "Off the top of my head, I don't remember that, but I would certainly discuss it with them."
  • Glenn Kukla, Kukla Capital Partners: asked about Petrobras satisfaction and future PRM; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "we are in good standing with them" and "I think overall... they're satisfied with where we're at in the project" while adding "they have not made any announcements publicly about any future plans."
  • Glenn Kukla, Kukla Capital Partners: asked if GEOS is a going concern in 24 months; President, CEO & Director Kelley: "Absolutely. Yes. We feel very good about fiscal year '27 and the opportunities we have going to fiscal year '28" and noted "One large caveat" around geopolitics.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: negative to slightly negative, concentrated on liquidity and survivability, highlighted by Michael Cox stating, "there's a definite risk that has been raised of is this company going to survive" and pressing that Q2 "feels like a long ways away" given Petrobras milestone timing.
  • Management: slightly positive in prepared remarks and more defensive in liquidity exchanges; President, CEO & Director Kelley repeatedly emphasized production progress and milestones, including "we are in full production now" and "we anticipate a cash infusion in early Q2," while also acknowledging constraints: "until we hit that milestone, we can't expect another infusion of cash."
  • Versus prior quarter: the current call contained more direct analyst pressure on debt availability and contingency planning; management responses leaned more toward bridging liquidity and confirming continuity, including "Absolutely. Yes" to the going-concern question.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • PRM execution framing shifted from Q3’s "lower than was expected due to customer requested changes" and an anticipated completion "between our fiscal Q3 and fiscal Q4 of next year" to Q4’s cadence discussion: "peak in our Q2 and come to an end in Q3" and "product-related revenue recognized by the end of fiscal year 2027." (President, CEO & Director Kelley; Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • Liquidity discussion intensified from Q3’s focus on cash management and credit facility support ("make it through to when we expect to get our next milestone payment") to Q4’s detailed dialogue about borrowing-base limits and contingency options "not off the table." (Executive VP, CFO & Secretary Curda)
  • Smart Water strategy evolved from product positioning in Q3 ("release of the Series V connector") to Q4’s channel shift: "ended a decade-long relationship" and "use internal sales and marketing resources" to pursue utility specifications. (President, CEO & Director Kelley)

Risks and Concerns

  • "Uncertainty and delays driven by ongoing changes in trade policy, a major Middle East energy disruption, continued sanctions and shifts in borrowing costs" were cited as constraints on operating in the company’s "current structure." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • Liquidity and milestone timing risk remained a central topic, with management linking near-term cash to PRM milestones: "until we hit that milestone, we can't expect another infusion of cash." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)
  • Segment-specific demand risks included Smart Water "slower hardware shipments" and Energy Solutions headwinds from "increased competition and consolidation" and "decreased demand for ocean bottom nodes." (President, CEO & Director Kelley)

Final Takeaway

Management tied its fiscal 2027 improvement narrative to restructuring actions, PRM execution and milestone cash timing, and a stated "backlog exceeding $100 million" while reiterating it would not provide formal guidance. In Q&A, analysts centered on liquidity, revolver constraints, and the risk of bridging to Petrobras milestone payments; management responded that it is "in full production now," expects a Petrobras cash infusion "in early Q2," and maintained that Geospace is a going concern: "Absolutely. Yes."

data.title: Praxis a new Buy at B Riley on cusp of potential approval for two therapies
data.description:
• B Riley initiated Praxis Precision Medicines (PRAX) at Buy, saying that the company may soon have two drug approvals in its hands with FDA action dates coming up in December and January for, respectively, relutrigine and ulixacaltamide.
  • The firm has a price target of $713 (~129% upside based on Nov. 19 close).
  • Analyst Madison El-Saadi said that ulixacaltamide, for essential tremor, has blockbuster potential given that the movement disorder is 10 times more prevalent than Parkinson's disease "yet neglected by drug developers for decades."
  • He sees ulixacaltamide achieving a more than $1B annual run rate by the end of 2027, compared to the Street consensus of 2029.
  • El-Saadi has "high conviction" the therapy will be approved by its PDUFA date of Jan. 29, adding he believes that the Street is underestimating ulixacaltamide, as Praxis will have around 300 sales reps targeting around 19,000 prescribers.
  • Relutrigine, which would treat SCN2A/SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, has a Dec. 27 PDUFA date. El-Saadi noted that the candidate's chances of approval were bolstered by the registrational cohort of the EMBOLD trial, which was stopped early due to efficacy.

data.title: NextEra-Dominion merger cleared by DoJ antitrust division
data.description:
The U.S. Justice ​Department's antitrust division ‌has cleared the $66.8B merger of NextEra Energy (NEE) and ​Dominion Energy (D), after noting concerns about the deal's potential impact on electricity costs, the DoJ said Thursday.

The companies' commitment to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to eliminate their unilateral right to deactivate units in New England "will protect consumers in the region from potentially hundreds of millions of dollars of increased electricity cost," the DoJ said.

In light of the commitment to FERC, the antitrust division decided that its investigation could be closed.

The Virginia State Corporation Commission must also approve the merger, and opening arguments in the state regulator's legal review of the deal began Tuesday.

The proposed merger, announced in May, would create the world's largest regulated electric utility, with a 130 GW large load pipeline, but clean energy groups and Virginia officials have raised concerns about the potential impact of the deal on rates and data center development.

Virginia Governor Spanberger reiterated her earlier demands for a six-year rate freeze, tripling bill credits for families and small businesses, and stronger protections to ensure data centers pay for their energy costs, but the companies rejected the demand for a rate freeze.

The state regulator said this week it will admit into evidence a memorandum alleging NextEra's (NEE) Florida Power and Light business interfered in Florida elections and politics; the company said in June it agreed to pay $150M to settle investor claims related to the allegations.

data.title: KKR in talks to buy majority stake in EdgeCore - report
data.description:
KKR & Co. (KKR) unit Helix Digital Infrastructure is in talks to acquire a majority stake in EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

The operator of high-density, hyperscale data centers built for cloud and AI workloads could be valued between $8B and $10B, according to one of the sources.

Helix is expected to buy the stake from Partners Group Holding, said the people, asking not to be identified because the information is confidential.

data.title: Fed shouldn’t hike again after December – OnePoint BFG Wealth’s Peter Boockvar
data.description:
The Federal Reserve should not raise interest rates again after December, said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer of OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners.

He cited turmoil in the AI tech trade, declining industrial metals prices, and falling crude oil prices (CL1:COM).

"I just don't see how the Fed will hike again after December, if they even do then, if this selloff and AI CapEx concerns continue," he said.

The investment strategist pointed to the outsized role that artificial intelligence plays in the current economy as the reason for the Fed to exercise caution. Data center construction accounts for roughly half of GDP growth, AI-related companies represent approximately half of the S&P 500's (SP500) market capitalization, and the sector drives about 75% of earnings growth.

He noted that upper-income consumers are heavily dependent on the wealth effect from a stock market largely propelled by the AI trade.

"If the economic contribution from the data center build wasn't about half of GDP growth, if it wasn't about half the S&P 500 in terms of market cap, if it wasn't about 75% of earnings growth right now, and if the upper-income U.S. consumer wasn't so dependent on the wealth effect of a higher stock market mostly being driven by the AI trade, I'd say the Fed can look past this all with their inflation focus, but that's not where we stand," Boockvar explained.

While he expressed confidence that Kevin Warsh is monitoring these developments, he suggested some Fed colleagues "aren't reading the full room."

Peter Tchir, head of Macro Strategy at Academy Securities, echoed similar concerns about monetary policy tightening.

"They should probably avoid hiking in December too," he said, reinforcing the broader skepticism among market strategists about near-term rate increases.

data.title: Playboy to exit Russell 3000 in December reconstitution
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of additions and deletions to its Russell 3000 index. The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the US markets close on December 11.

The Russell 3000 Index tracks the performance of the 3,000 largest U.S. companies and is designed to represent roughly 98% of the investable U.S. equity market.

No consumer staples company will be added to the index during the latest reshuffle, while Playboy (PLBY) is the only stock being deleted.

data.title: North Dakota oil producers moving crude by truck as pipeline outage continues
data.description:
North Dakota oil producers are moving crude by truck as a prolonged outage of Enbridge's (ENB) pipeline in the state forces them to seek alternatives to avoid shutting in production.

"Some producers and marketers are trucking out production to delivery points on the Dakota Access Pipeline," Energy Aspects' head of global crude Jeremy Irwin told Bloomberg in an interview Friday. "Their tanks are filling up, and they can't get enough trucks to evacuate the Bakken crude they have, which could potentially lead to production shut-ins."

The North Dakota Pipeline, which delivers as much as 465K bbl/day of light, sweet crude to Canada and U.S. refineries, has been operating at lower rates since last week after a surge in reports of tainted crude forced Enbridge (ENB) to implement testing for organic chlorides, slowing down the system.

It is unclear when the pipeline will resume normal production, and Energy Aspects said the source of the contamination must be identified and addressed before the system can fully restart.

Demand for Bakken alternatives from Canadian fields is increasing, reportedly prompting Enbridge (ENB) to tell customers it will cut requested light crude shipments at Kerrobert, Saskatchewan, by 24% in December, the highest apportionment since February.

Marathon Petroleum's MPLX midstream arm reportedly issued a force majeure on North Dakota oil pipeline deliveries earlier this week.
